title: Desloppify with Crowdfunding
author: CheddarGoblinDev
selftext:
So I finally have to admit - thanks to AI I can realistically bring ideas to an end or at least to a desired milestone. So I don't have to say to myself "Nice idea - but maybe I can work on this in my 70s".

However I still can't feel the generated Art. With code it's something different. If it works it works. Art has to turn more subtle knobs for the viewer.

So I thought to myself; I can build the game, deliver it and at the same time ask on Kickstarter (and so) if people would support and donate the projects in terms of desloppification.

The idea is that Crowdfunding does not need to support the project for its completion anymore but to make it more *human*.

In my head this feels right. It kinda mends the deep cut AI cause to artists especially in the game industry.

What do you think?

comments.author: niloony
comments.body: People prefer to pay talented artists and teams directly to make their vision. Rather than give it to some guy who will outsource it to make his vision look a bit better or worse but they paid someone.

replies.author: CheddarGoblinDev
replies.body:
I don't fully understand what you mean? The thing with Crowdfunding is lack of financial resources. If I would have had the cash in the first place I definitely would go for real artists since I always honour the work of a good one.

You said something about outsourcing - can you elaborate on that?

replies.author: cowman3456
replies.body: You are trying to outsource art, with an incomplete, or weak, vertical slice.  The market is crowded.  Crowd sourcing this would likely be challenging.

comments.author: egonosz
comments.body:
What you bring to table in this case? 

If I would check the page, what would make me fund your game? 

The first thing I would check, if I think this person is able to actually deliver in acceptable quality.

replies.author: CheddarGoblinDev
replies.body:
Yeah so in my case I would have a game already launched and ready to play. However it still contains AI generated assets that in my idea act as a placeholder and are waiting to be swapped out with Human-Made art.

The Kickstarter (example) campaign would emphasize on the fact that the projects is already done - at least people can see it's not about the completion of the project anymore but - as I said at the top - about desloppifing it from AI art.

replies.author: ipreuss
replies.body: I think it could work well if you already have an artist and could show before / after examples.

comments.author: ichivictus
comments.body:
Nobody is going to fund a kickstarter to turn an ai slop in a game into human art.

But a better idea is to have multiple artists that use ai to join the project. AI can produce great art, it just needs to be intentional and iterated on. It still takes an artistic eye to 'deslopify' it but it can be done quickly by people who know what they are doing. I make my steam capsule art with ai and have gotten compliments and no accusations.

  
I was considering a similar idea.  A place where ai devs, artists, etc. can find each other's projects and join and earn a percentage of the sales as a partner or hired per project or work for free if the game will be free. A place where AI power users can post their portfolio and find people who might be interested in joining your project.

  
Problem with that is that it makes the game known as an ai assisted game and opens the door to anti-ai folk harassing but I think the tides are beginning to turn in favor of indies using ai finally.

comments.author: Jolly-Rip5973
comments.body:
You can make excellent high quality images with AI but;

1) You kind of need some talent or education in art to have good artistic judgment.   
2) you may need to use advanced models to control complex composition.   
3) you may need to train and use LoRA files to control style and consistency across a large set of images.   
4) you may need to combine it with traditional digital editing tool to clean up errors.   
5) you will probably need a multi-stage workflow if you really to maximize quality. 

Most professional gaming studio are using Ai tools now even generative Ai tools by the gen Ai is being used by professional artists and they are combining it with traditional digital media tools. 

I've done professional graphics design for many years. I can also use advanced Ai tool even creating datasets and fine tuning or create LoRAs files for generative models.  
  
If I were doing artwork for a game, it would professional projects where there was quality control and correct with each and every asset and it would take time.   
  
The main problem a lot of vibecorder have is that they trying to automate everything.   
  
It's all the little human decisions that go into a professional workflow that make a good product.   
  
If you automate all the human decisions out of the process; you get slop.   
  
People have this concept that Ai tool replace professionals.   
No, Ai becomes tools for professionals that know what they doing.   
   
[https://www.thegamer.com/game-studios-using-generative-ai-claude-in-development/](https://www.thegamer.com/game-studios-using-generative-ai-claude-in-development/)

Over 85 percent of Japanese game developers actively use generative artificial intelligence (AI) to streamline production, according to data from the Computer Entertainment Supplier's Association (CESA).

Adoption Rates and Usage

* **Surging Adoption:** A CESA industry survey released at the Tokyo Game Show reveals that 85.8% of Japanese game developers use generative AI, a massive jump from just 51% the previous year.
* **Daily Workflow:** Approximately 63% of surveyed developers use AI tools daily, while 22.8% use them occasionally.
* **Prominent Studios:** Major CESA member companies embracing these workflows include industry heavyweights like Capcom, Sega, Konami, and Level-5.
* **Quality Control:** Most studios enforce strict limitations, relying heavily on human supervision, verification, and correction to avoid using direct, unedited AI-generated art or text in final releases.
